text: Cómbita is a town and municipality located in the Colombian Department of Boyacá, within the Central Boyacá Province subregion. It lies on the Altiplano Cundiboyacense and shares borders with Arcabuco and the department of Santander to the north, Sotaquirá to the northeast, Tuta and Oicatá to the east, the department capital Tunja, which is 8.5 kilometres (5.3 mi) away, to the west and south, and both Arcabuco and Motavita to the west. Prior to the arrival of the Spanish conquistadors, the area was inhabited by the Muisca people, who were organized into the Muisca Confederation. The northern Muisca were ruled by the zaque of Hunza, corresponding to modern-day Tunja, and the cacique of Cómbita was a loyal subject of the zaque. In the Chibcha language spoken by the Muisca, the name Cómbita means either "Hand of the jaguar and wheel of life" or "Force of the summit." Modern Cómbita was officially founded in 1586. The primary economic activities in the town include agriculture, specifically the cultivation of potatoes, barley, wheat, maize, and peas, as well as livestock farming. Its geographic coordinates are 5°45′N 73°15′W (5.750°N 73.250°W).
